headline: Xbox cuts 268 jobs as Activision takes over Halo development
summary: Ninja Theory faces closure as Xbox consolidates studios and restructures its first-party development teams.
details: Xbox is laying off 268 employees as part of a broader studio consolidation and efficiency drive. The cuts impact Halo Studios and other first-party developers, as well as management and central functions.

The latest job cuts follow a July layoff of 1,600 employees. Xbox Executive Vice President Matt Booty stated that these actions bring the company roughly three-quarters of the way through its previously announced restructuring.
Activision will now be responsible for developing the next Halo game, with a small team remaining to support existing titles. Activision will also oversee Rare and World's Edge.
Obsidian is moving under Bethesda, while King will manage Microsoft Casual Games. Playground Games and Turn 10 Studios are merging to focus on Forza and Fable.

Compulsion Games and Double Fine Productions have been spun out as independent studios with funding and IP rights. Undead Labs has also been divested, though State of Decay 3 remains slated for Game Pass.

Efforts to sell Ninja Theory have failed, leading to a proposed closure of the studio. Xbox is also in a consultation period for Arkane Studios in Lyon, with potential outcomes including sale, spin-out, or closure, expected to conclude by the end of 2026.

headline_marked: Apple adds [[persistent 'ads']] to iOS Settings, frustrating users
headline: Apple adds persistent 'ads' to iOS Settings, frustrating users
summary: Prompts for paid services like iCloud+ and AppleCare+ are appearing in the Settings app, with limited options to dismiss them.
details: Apple is reportedly inserting promotional content for its own services, including iCloud+ storage, Apple Music, Apple TV free trials, and AppleCare+ warranties, directly into the iOS Settings app.

Users are expressing frustration as these 'ads' can be difficult to dismiss, with some taking weeks or months to expire and leaving persistent notification badges. In many cases, there is no 'dismiss' button, and when one is present, some users report it doesn't work.
This move has drawn comparisons to Microsoft's introduction of ads in the Windows Start menu, with users lamenting the perceived degradation of the Apple user experience.
While Apple has long emphasized its premium brand and user experience, this strategy aligns with its increasing focus on services revenue amidst slowing smartphone market growth.
Some users suspect a bug, particularly those already subscribed to iCloud+, are still seeing these promotions. However, if the ads persist, it suggests a deliberate strategy rather than an error.
With Apple reportedly planning similar promotions for other systems, such as its Visual Intelligence system, users may need to brace for more in-app advertising.
